# HOUZEIFY SCREEN CLASSIFICATION (TABLE B - phases B01 + B03)

**Baseline described:** `main` @ `71f1090` (TABLE A). **Type:** documents only - no source, server, schema or config file was changed to produce this report. Generated by script from the TABLE A auditors' per-screen tables (`scratchpad/audit/A-screens-routes.md`, A03/A04/A06/A28; `C-data-homeservices-historical-docs-boq.md`, A08/A18/A19) plus a fresh import-graph pass over a read-only `git archive 71f1090` snapshot of `src/` (280 `.ts/.tsx` files, 337 files total, 0 unresolved imports, no dynamic `import()` in `src/`). The worktree was not read for any table cell, so concurrent edits by other agents cannot skew it.

**After TABLE B:** the classification and reachability columns describe the TABLE A baseline; the *TABLE B action* column records what this branch did to each screen (hidden, archived, shell change). Post-change results are in `HOUZEIFY_POST_LEGACY_CLEANUP_AUDIT.md`.

Statement labels: **FACT** (verified in code / by script), **RECOMMENDATION** (advice for later TABLE B phases; never an instruction to delete), **UNKNOWN**. Evidence is `path:line` relative to the repo root. Classification vocabulary (only these appear in the table): `KEEP, MODIFY, SHARED, COMING SOON, HIDE, ARCHIVE, DELETE CANDIDATE, LEGACY INTERNAL, UNKNOWN`.

## Contents
1. Deletion-risk rubric and column definitions
2. B03 PRODUCT BOUNDARY (ACTIVE / SECONDARY / LEGACY-HIDDEN lists, naming collisions, boundary rules, straddlers)
3. B01 master classification table (169 route-id rows + 5 unrouted rows)
4. Embedded section components (not counted as screens)
5. Verification (recounts) and TABLE A disagreements

## 1. Deletion-risk rubric and column definitions

Deletion risk = how likely deleting or moving **this file** is to break something else. Computed by script from the fresh import graph (importers, literal/constant route-id references from active files, and writes to shared stores). It is a screening aid, **not** a deletion instruction.

| Level | Rule (first matching reason wins upward; the highest level reached is used) |
|---|---|
| HIGH | (a) class is KEEP / MODIFY / SHARED (an active 2.0 or shared screen); or (b) the file is imported by an ACTIVE screen or an active shared component (file-level break); or (c) one component backs several route ids, at least one of them an active nav placeholder (`ComingSoonScreen`); or (d) the file owns a store consumed by active code (only data modules - no screen file owns one). |
| MEDIUM | No active importer, but at least one of: (a) imported by another non-active screen (family-internal or cross-family - must move/delete as a set); (b) its route id is literally referenced or reached through a `*_ROUTES` constant by an ACTIVE screen, active shell (`Sidebar`, `PartnerNavRail`, `ProjectSubNav`) or an active route-config data file (dangling-link risk); (c) it WRITES (calls a create/add/award/update/set/save/... function of) a legacy or shared store that active screens also read (removing it changes what an active screen shows); (d) it is a SECONDARY (Business Development) screen - the product stays. |
| LOW | Only `App.tsx` imports it (import + render block + union member + switcher entry), no active nav reference, and it writes no store that an active screen reads. |

Every routed screen also has a live reference in `src/App.tsx` (import, `AppScreen` union member, render block). That wiring is the same for all 169 ids, so it is not counted as a risk factor; it is what makes every routed screen non-deletable as-is (see the DELETE-candidate verification in `HOUZEIFY_LEGACY_DEPENDENCY_TRACE.md`).

**Columns.** `#` = App.tsx render order (1-169) then the 5 unrouted files (170-174). `name` = component. `route id` = `AppScreen` id (one row per id; `ComingSoonScreen` backs 10 ids so it has 10 rows). `product area` = TABLE B area (sub-area in brackets). `boundary` (extra column) = B03 list: ACTIVE / SECONDARY / LEGACY-HIDDEN. `reachability` = TABLE A class (A06). `API dependency` = backend endpoints from the audit plus any `*Api`/real-backend module the file imports. `data dependency` = TABLE A source class + the `src/data` stores it imports, grouped real (talks to the backend) / local (in-memory store or React context) / mock (static fixture, catalogue, config or create*/validate service). `shared dependency` = imports (shared components and `src/data` stores) that at least one OTHER active screen also uses, as `name(n)` where n = number of other active consumers (direct or through another data module); the `HIcon` icon component is omitted (136 importers). `TABLE B action` is intentionally blank.

| Sub-area | Screen ids | Data modules | Backend |

| Opportunities / Discover Projects | `discover-projects`, `project-opportunity-detail` | projectOpportunities (always empty: createProjectOpportunity has 0 callers), professionalType, documentUpload | none (frontend-only) |
| Bids | `submit-bid`, `bid-submitted`, `my-bids` | bids (createBid at SubmitBidScreen), invitations, documentUpload; identityVerification gates access (PartnerNavRail Opportunities lock) | none (frontend-only, in-memory) |

**FACT.** These screens are TABLE A `LEGACY INTERNAL` (A28) and sit on the company rail under the demoted 'Business Development' section (PartnerNavRail.tsx:145-146); their data is entirely in-memory (`bids.ts`, `projectOpportunities.ts`, `invitations.ts`), with no server route or table. `createProjectOpportunity` has 0 callers, so Discover Projects can only show its empty state; a bid can only start from a homeowner invitation created in the same tab (`InviteContractorScreen.tsx`, the LEGACY marketplace side). **RECOMMENDATION:** keep the screens; treat `bids.ts`/`invitations.ts`/`projectOpportunities.ts` as the SECONDARY-owned modules and stop ACTIVE code reading them (section 2.6, rule R2).

### 2.6 Boundary rules (what may import what)

RECOMMENDATION rules for the target state; each row also states the FACT count of current violations (from the import graph and route-reference pass).

| # | Rule | Current state (FACT) |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | ACTIVE screens and active shells must NOT import LEGACY-family `src/data` modules or LEGACY screens/components (`user/new-build`, `user/renovation`, `user/home-services`). | 16 import edges from 6 ACTIVE screens into LEGACY stores (agreements x1, customerAddress x2, customerBooking x1, estimateVersions x3, houseRequirements x2, houseRequirementsState x1, payments x2, projects x3, serviceEntry x1); 1 active -> legacy component import: `HomeDashboardScreen.tsx:10` `SelectAServiceSection`; plus 1 shared component -> legacy store: `AddressPickerModal.tsx:15` -> `customerAddress`. |
| R2 | ACTIVE code must NOT read SECONDARY-owned stores (`bids`, `invitations`, `projectOpportunities`, `contractorDirectory`); SECONDARY screens may use them; the dependency must never point from ACTIVE to them (SECONDARY -> bids is allowed, ACTIVE -> bids is not). | 17 import edges from 11 ACTIVE screens into SECONDARY stores (bids x6, contractorDirectory x10, invitations x1). |
| R3 | ACTIVE screens must NOT navigate by literal id (or `*_ROUTES` constant) to LEGACY/SECONDARY screens, except through one declared 'legacy entry' config that TABLE B can switch off. `home-services-coming-soon` is the sanctioned placeholder target. | 73 navigation references from ACTIVE files (screens, Sidebar/PartnerNavRail, route configs) to LEGACY or SECONDARY ids (excluding the placeholder); largest fan-outs: `homeownerDashboard.ts` (DASHBOARD_ROUTES), `aiAdvisor.ts`, `Sidebar.tsx`, `HomeDashboardScreen.tsx`. |
| R4 | LEGACY / SECONDARY code MAY import ACTIVE core (real-backend clients/providers, `constructionStages`, shared shell components) - the allowed direction is legacy -> active. Legacy code must not WRITE into ACTIVE stores except through the public API hooks. | Only `RenovateProjectCreatedScreen.tsx:105` (`projects.createProject` -> real Postgres project, then seeds legacy `createBid`/`awardBid`) and `HouseRequirementsScreen.tsx:344-345,357` (POST/PATCH /projects via `projects.createProject/updateProject`, PUT /requirements via `houseRequirementsCache.save`) cross into the real backend from legacy screens. |
| R5 | LEGACY data modules must not import ACTIVE data modules, and ACTIVE data modules must not import LEGACY ones. | 15 cross-family data-module edges: `projects.ts -> bids.ts` (LEGACY -> SECONDARY, this is how bids reach 3 active screens), `houseRequirementsState/Api -> authState/apiClient` (legacy -> active, allowed), `bids/projectOpportunities -> documentUpload`, `contractorDirectory -> accountType/organizationSetup/professionalType/serviceCategories`, `aiAdvisor -> homeownerDashboard`, `boqFormat -> constructionStages`, `projectDocumentsApi -> projectDocumentsStore`. |
| R6 | Shared shells (`Sidebar`, `PartnerNavRail`, `homeownerDashboard.ts` `DASHBOARD_ROUTES`) must not carry destinations for LEGACY screens for users of company projects; they are ACTIVE files and should point only at ACTIVE ids (or the coming-soon placeholder). | `Sidebar.tsx:238,257-261,270`; `homeownerDashboard.ts:36-50` (8 legacy keys: buildOrImprove, renovate, createProject, findContractors, bidsReceived, estimateDashboard, boqOverview, uploadPlan; homeServices is the placeholder) + Hozie ladders; `PartnerNavRail.tsx:145-146` (SECONDARY - allowed). |
| R7 | App-level providers must be ACTIVE-only. | `CustomerCartProvider` and `CustomerAddressProvider` (Home Services state) wrap the entire app: `App.tsx:1005-1006` (+ imports :128-129). |
| R8 | Assets: ACTIVE screens must not import from `src/imports/Services icons` / `Hoziehelper`. | `HomeDashboardScreen.tsx:8-14` imports 6 Services-icons PNGs (4 also used by Home Services screens); `BuildOrImproveScreen.tsx:44-45` (legacy) imports 2 more. |
